findings.title: verify accepts an empty dataset and an empty or incomplete manifest file map
findings.evidence: Static reading of original verify: iterates only supplied manifest.files; iterates candidate rows without validating count, IDs, groups, cohorts or source correspondence. Therefore files={} and candidates=[] bypass both loops. Parent began fixing before dynamic reproduction completed.
findings.impact: A damaged or rewritten manifest can remove candidate validation and all source-to-build invariants while verify reports success.
findings.recommendation: Require exact manifest keys/file set and safe filenames, validate draft flags, candidate length/IDs/groups/cohorts, regenerate fixtures from current authoring, validate projection metadata, and compare rematerialized candidates and summary/review artifacts.

findings.title: verify does not establish current Node implementation or source-to-candidate lineage
findings.evidence: Exporter embeds hashes of six actual Node source dependencies in each projection, but Python verification never compares those hashes with the backend or verifies projection-input hashes/metadata; it only checks manifest-listed bytes.
findings.impact: Node code can change while unchanged Python build verification still succeeds; a candidate and self-rehashed manifest can diverge from the editable source. The existing current build did independently reproduce exactly.
findings.recommendation: Record and validate backend dependency hashes, offer backend-aware verification or explicitly report snapshot-only verification, recompute projection hashes, and rematerialize candidate records from source and checked projection.

findings.title: manifest-level draft and human-review claims are unchecked
findings.evidence: Original code has no checks for manifest status/version/model/review flags; it checks only candidate-level eligibility and human review inside the per-row loop.
findings.impact: Consumers relying on manifest metadata can see claims that the validator never enforces.
findings.recommendation: Validate the manifest draft status and exact false flags; retain explicit AI synthetic provenance and separate independent AI review from human review.

observations: Existing build is reproducible against real current Node exporter, not a handwritten Python imitation.
Only component-message-only removes application_id/status_code; planned cohort explicitly changes profile and knowledge collections; preauth remains visibly separate.
Build refuses an already existing output directory; Node exporter validates all rows before exclusive output write. Failed builds can leave a partial new directory, which correctly cannot be reused.
Wrapper exposes only build/verify/audit. Optional audit loads a local tokenizer, never trains or promotes eligibility.
Synthetic origin/licence statement is an author declaration, not proof of originality or human review.
A manifest stored beside writable files is not an adversarial signature; a separately trusted digest or immutable store is required for authenticity.
